title: Perplexity Masters Class
description: A full Perplexity apprenticeship: cited research loops, source triage, claim verification, note systems, brief writing, and turning web answers into trustworthy decisions end to end.

lessons.title: Perplexity as a Research Copilot

introduction.text: Perplexity shines when you need answers grounded in current web sources with citations you can open. It is not a substitute for reading primary material on high-stakes claims. Your apprenticeship goal is a repeatable research loop: question → sources → triage → notes → brief—not screenshotting the first answer.

options: Cited answers from web sources you can inspect
questions.correctAnswer: Cited answers from web sources you can inspect

questions.question: A research loop should end in:
options: Notes or a brief you can defend
questions.correctAnswer: Notes or a brief you can defend

lessons.title: Query Design for Better Sources

introduction.text: Sharp queries name the entity, timeframe, geography, and desired evidence type (stats, docs, reviews, papers). Use follow-ups to narrow. Ask for contrasting viewpoints when the topic is contested. Bad queries get SEO sludge; good queries invite primary-ish sources.

options: Prefer the kind of material you need
questions.correctAnswer: Prefer the kind of material you need

questions.question: Follow-ups are for:
options: Narrowing scope with what you learned
questions.correctAnswer: Narrowing scope with what you learned

lessons.title: Source Triage and Credibility

introduction.text: Not all citations are equal. Triage by primary vs secondary, date, author incentives, and methodological clarity. Prefer official docs, papers, and reputable reporting for hard claims. Use Perplexity to gather candidates—then you rank them.

lessons.title: Claim Extraction and Verification

introduction.text: Break answers into atomic claims. For each claim, record source, quote/paraphrase, and verification status (confirmed / contested / unsupported). This turns chat into an audit trail. Escalate contested claims to primary documents or subject experts.

questions.question: Unsupported means:
options: No adequate source backs the claim
questions.correctAnswer: No adequate source backs the claim

lessons.title: Notes, Briefs, and Knowledge Capture

introduction.text: Convert verified findings into durable notes: question, answer, sources, confidence, and next actions. Briefs for stakeholders should lead with the decision-relevant point, then evidence. Capture “what I still don’t know” so future you continues the thread.

questions.correctAnswer: How hard to lean on the finding

lessons.title: Research Ops for Teams

introduction.text: Standardize how your team asks, verifies, and files Perplexity work: query patterns, triage scorecards, claim ledgers, and brief templates. Define SLAs for “good enough” vs “publishable.” Teach juniors the difference between speed and rigor.
